authoring: Source-history-informed retrospective instrument. This original contract was written after source/executor history and before candidate discovery. Any outcome-informed narrower facet must preserve this file.
deduplication: Stable repository entity ID and closure-event identity; one delivered closure per entity lifetime, assigned only to its first qualifying closure interval. Reopening is a separately reported safeguard, never another delivery.
population: Bounded, discovery-selected public outputs; not a census of eligible opportunities. Periods outside retained native evidence remain null, never zero.
workflowContribution: A comment/marker is discovery or corroboration, not a creation receipt. Receipt-qualified attribution requires run identity, workflow source at the run SHA, and actual safe-output application targeting the same entity and transition.
decision: Not rated: no agreed native keep bar. No dollars or causation.

stale-pr-cleanup.goal: Reduce the 30+ day stale PR backlog without discarding genuine work.
stale-pr-cleanup.originalAcceptance: An open PR with pre-action updatedAt older than 30 days and no keep-open, blocked, awaiting-review, do-not-close or hold label is correctly classified in A/B/C order and closed unmerged, with the source-required comment and label. Human non-draft ambiguity defaults to warning; maintainer/admin closure needs superseded evidence.
stale-pr-cleanup.nativeFacet: Independently verified source-eligible unmerged stale PR closures. Source eligibility, draft/bot status as applicable, label history and the actual closure transition must be established independently of the cleanup comment.
stale-pr-cleanup.safeguards: Correct classification precedence, role protection, communications, reopen behavior and full opportunity coverage are separate from the native closure facet.
stale-pr-cleanup.ruleHistory: 30-day threshold and A/B/C/D classification unchanged since adoption. Later changes affect imports, engine, transport, runtime and reporting, not eligibility.

draft-pr-cleanup.goal: Retire inactive draft PRs to reduce clutter and triage burden.
draft-pr-cleanup.originalAcceptance: An open draft with no keep-draft, blocked or awaiting-review label and at least 14 days since ALL relevant activity is closed unmerged after warning, retaining stale-draft and a helpful closure comment. Activity includes commits, comments, label changes, review requests/reviews and title/body updates.
draft-pr-cleanup.nativeFacet: Independently verified source-eligible inactive draft PR closures. Historical draft state, actual inactivity and exemption state, and open-to-closed-unmerged transition are required independently of the cleanup comment.
draft-pr-cleanup.safeguards: Warning timing, complete communication, draft-rate goal, full opportunity coverage and subsequent reopens remain separately assessed.
draft-pr-cleanup.ruleHistory: 10-13-day warning and 14+-day closure policy unchanged since adoption. 2026-10-14 disables shell routes and requires native MCP permission handling; it does not retroactively change eligibility.

sub-issue-closer.goal: Close open parent issues whose nonempty sub-issue set is 100% closed, bottom-up.
sub-issue-closer.originalAcceptance: A nonempty, complete historical parent-child graph immediately before closure has every child closed. The parent transitions from open to closed/completed, receives a correct explanatory comment, and recursive ancestors are processed bottom-up within limits.
sub-issue-closer.nativeFacet: Verified parent closures after every member of its nonempty historical child set closed. Graph membership and all child lifecycle timestamps must be independently established; a task-list or self-reported completion count is insufficient.
sub-issue-closer.safeguards: Communication, recursion completeness, run limits and all eligible opportunity coverage remain separate.
sub-issue-closer.ruleHistory: All nonempty children closed remains the rule since adoption. Tool transport, reporting and Copilot-to-Codex-to-Pi engine changes are not new goal activations.
